statement: Find the tangent to $y=x^{3}-3x$ at $x=2$, and show it meets the curve again at $(-4,-52)$.
solution: At $x=2$, $y=2$ and $y'=3x^{2}-3=9$. Tangent: $y-2=9(x-2)$, i.e. $y=9x-16$. Intersection: $x^{3}-3x=9x-16\Rightarrow x^{3}-12x+16=0$. Since $x=2$ is a root, $(x-2)(x^{2}+2x-8)=(x-2)^{2}(x+4)=0$, so the other intersection is $x=-4$, $y=9(-4)-16=-52$.
hints: Differentiate to get the gradient at $x=2$.
Solve $x^{3}-3x=9x-16$ and factor out the known root $x=2$.
